correctness.rationale: The exact inverse-swap clause law follows by an explicit bijection from selections of 01 junctions to predecessor words. Each clause is bounded by a cyclic vertex-cover constraint, whose number is Lucas L_t. Even extremizers require all unit runs; odd extremizers have precisely one doubled run and a forced vertex yielding F_(k+1) path covers. The n=7 coarse-bound tie and n<=3 bijective cases are separately resolved. Executed direct exhaustive forward maps through n=18, separate inverse-swap comparisons through n=14, and transfer-matrix evaluations through n=200. Finite tests do not replace the all-length proof.

evidence: Powley 2009 Chapter 4 and Section 9.3, especially the trace of a product of symbol-conditioned de Bruijn matrices (Equations 9.32-9.34), give exact predecessor counts for any specified cyclic output, with no computational savings when the period equals the ring length.
Fukś 1999 specializes to preimages of blocks of zeros and flow, rather than maximization over cyclic outputs.

Jen 1989 Section 3 classifies Rule 184 among Fibonacci-type finite-block preimage recurrences, and Section 5.4 discusses maximizing probabilities of finite blocks for selected different rules; no Rule 184 cyclic-ring maximum is asserted there.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Pointwise target-counting algorithms subsume computation of any fixed target, but do not logically imply an analytic all-length maximum or equality classification without comparing exponentially many target patterns. The new proof supplies that nontrivial comparison.

originality.rationale: The claimed contribution is optimization of predecessor number over all indexed cyclic target words at each size, and classification of all maximizers. Jen 1989 gives arbitrary finite-block counting and studies maximal probability for other specific rules, not the Rule 184 cyclic extremizers; Fukś 1997/1999 addresses specific finite-block preimages and traffic flow, Evans/Rajewsky/Speer 1998 studies open-boundary stochastic traffic, and Powley 2009 provides pointwise de Bruijn transfer matrices (including heterogeneous cyclic targets) but no theorem optimizing those counts simultaneously for Rule 184 or classifying extremizers in examined material. The general pointwise transfer method and Lucas cover numbers are acknowledged prior tools, not independently novel claims. Residual historical priority risk remains.
residual_risks: An unpublished or unindexed finite-state traffic study might state the same all-length maximum and equality patterns.
Classical Lucas counting for a chosen alternating output is elementary, so novelty is restricted to the global bound and complete equality classification.
Full PDF page-image inspection of the Powley thesis was unavailable; the relevant text was inspected via accessible extraction.

value.rationale: The worst one-step inverse ambiguity for a ubiquitous deterministic particle-conserving cyclic traffic model is a natural and operationally meaningful invariant. The formula is exact for every length, supplies a matching sharp upper bound and equality classification, and reveals a parity-dependent transition from two perfectly alternating maximizers to 2n once-defective ones. This is not merely a finite census, known-table recomputation or one-target Lucas recurrence.
